decisions.reason: The Definition specifies a policy and asserts no confidence-coverage or regret guarantee. After initialization every count is positive; real rewards give finite empirical means, delta in (0,1) gives a positive finite logarithm, and finite least-index maximization defines each next action using only revealed history. These operations remain valid for integrable heavy-tailed rewards. The separate expected-pull and regret statements explicitly assume 1-sub-Gaussian entries. The book's statistical assumption supports those guarantees, not a requirement for executing the procedure.

The Example and all three Verification steps correctly concern deterministic zero reward stacks, but the title omits that restriction and can suggest that tied means force zero realized reward regret. With two Bernoulli(1/2) arms at n=1 the realized quantity is 1/2-Y, equal to plus or minus 1/2, despite zero gaps. Renamed the item to Deterministic zero-reward arms have zero regret and mirrored that title in its owning manifest. The Example, proof, dependencies and strength are unchanged. This is a nonfatal presentation defect, not a false proof.

The four local UCB performance statements separately impose the necessary 1-sub-Gaussian hypothesis; none obtains it from the algorithm definition. No item, contract or page edit is needed.

Reviewed the fixed deterministic-zero Example, its model supplier, full Verification, contract and owning page. Each arm mean and gap is zero, every selected reward is zero, and both defining regret sums vanish pointwise; expectation then gives zero. Deterministic table entries satisfy independence, and n=1 is included. Only the overly broad title changed. The manifest title and three current boundary-review bindings were updated under the shared-write lock, preserving prior boundary evidence. This is repair-author checking, not independent review of the repair.
